question: In the shell-and-tube heat exchanger simulation with water (fine mesh), by what percentage did the heat transfer rate increase from 0.5 kg/s to 0.7 kg/s?

Heat Transfer Enhancement in a Shell-and-Tube Type of Heat Exchanger Using Al2O3/Water Nanofluid, page 3

Table 3 presents a comparison between the heat transfer rates obtained through numerical simulations and those derived from analytical methods, when the heat exchanger operates solely with water. 

The fine mesh was ultimately selected for the numerical simulations, as the number of elements compared to the coarser meshes did not entail a significant increase in computational cost, while offering improved accuracy in the results.

|  |  | C |  | 0.7 | 111.79 | 109.76 | 1.85 |  |
|  |  |  |  | 0.5 | 86.06 | 84.03 | 2.42 |  |
|  |  |  |  | 0.6 | 99.68 | 99.91 | 1.04 |  |

The heat transfer rate increased from 84.43 kW at 0.5 kg/s to 111.79 kW at 0.7 kg/s, which is an increase of 32.07% ((111.79 - 84.43) / 84.43).
